problem.title: Read a Table Pair
problem.statement: A table pairs time in minutes with distance in meters: (0, 0), (2, 5), (4, 10), and (6, 15). What distance corresponds to 4 minutes?
hints: Find the row whose first entry is 4 minutes.

solutionSteps.title: Read the paired row
solutionSteps.body: The pair (4, 10) means that at 4 minutes the distance is 10 meters.

validationMethods: Direct row lookup maps input 4 to output 10.
Independent proportional check: the table increases 5 meters per 2 minutes, so 4 minutes is two intervals and 2×5=10; only D matches.
notes: Units distinguish the input and output entries.

problem.title: Count the Axis Steps
problem.statement: A vertical graph axis is labeled 0, 25, 50, 75, 100 at equally spaced ticks. A point lies on the third tick above 0. What value does it represent?
hints: Count tick values, not just tick marks.

solutionSteps.title: Use the scale
solutionSteps.body: The ticks above 0 represent 25, 50, and 75. The third tick therefore represents 75.

validationMethods: Sequential tick reading gives 25, 50, 75 for the first three ticks above zero.
Independent multiplication check: three intervals ×25 units/interval =75; only D matches.
notes: The distractor 3 captures ignoring the scale.

problem.title: Match a Water-Level Story
problem.statement: A tank fills steadily for 4 minutes, remains unchanged for 2 minutes, and then drains steadily. Which graph description matches water level versus time?

choices.label: C
choices.text: rise continuously with no flat part

choices.label: E
choices.text: fall continuously with no flat part

hints: Translate each story interval into how the vertical water-level variable changes.

solutionSteps.title: Translate in order
solutionSteps.body: Filling increases level, unchanged level makes a horizontal segment, and draining decreases level. The shape is rise, flat, fall.

validationMethods: Clause-by-clause variable translation yields positive, zero, then negative change.
Independent option audit confirms only A preserves all three intervals and their order.
notes: The context differs from the race anchor.

problem.title: Extend a Constant Table
problem.statement: A table shows time in minutes 0, 2, 4, 6 and water added in liters 0, 3, 6, 9. If the same trend continues, how many liters have been added after 10 minutes?
hints: Every 2 minutes adds 3 liters; count intervals to 10 minutes.

solutionSteps.title: Continue the repeated change
solutionSteps.body: Ten minutes contains five 2-minute intervals. At 3 liters per interval, 5×3=15 liters are added.

validationMethods: Independent unit-rate check: 3/2=1.5 liters/minute and 1.5×10=15; only C matches.
notes: The table supports extension because a constant trend is stated.

problem.title: A Misleading Bar Scale
problem.statement: A bar chart's vertical axis starts at 90 instead of 0. One bar reaches 92 and another reaches 96, so the visible portion of the second bar is three times as tall as the first. Which statement correctly compares the actual values?

choices.label: C
choices.text: The values differ by 4, and 96 is about 4.3% greater than 92.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The values differ by 6 because the axis starts at 90.

problem.shortAnswer: They differ by 4; 96 is about 4.3% greater than 92.
hints: Compare the labeled values, not only the visible lengths above the truncated baseline.

solutionSteps.title: Read values before shapes
solutionSteps.body: The actual difference is 96−92=4. Relative to 92, the increase is 4/92≈0.0435, or about 4.3%. The truncated axis exaggerates the visual difference.

validationMethods: Independent ratio and option audit: 96/92≈1.0435, neither 2 nor 3; only C matches both the absolute and relative comparisons.
notes: The wording explains why visible bar fragments differ sharply without endorsing that visual ratio.
